records.text: Sword Guard (Tsuba). Japanese. Dated 1600–1700. Iron, copper. H. 4 1/2 in. (11.4 cm); W. 4 7/16 in. (11.3 cm); thickness 1/4 in. (0.6 cm); Wt. 7.2 oz. (204.1 g). Classified as Sword Furniture-Tsuba. From Japan. Gift of Bashford Dean, 1919.

records.title: Angel
records.text: Angel. Crèche figure. Giuseppe Gori. Dated second half 18th century. Polychromed terracotta head; wooden limbs and wings; body of wire wrapped in tow; various fabrics. H. 15 1/4 in. (38.7 cm.). Classified as Crèche. Gift of Loretta Hines Howard, 1964.

records.title: Piece
records.text: Piece. Dated ca. 1600. Silk. L. 24 1/2 x W. 9 inches (62.2 x 22.9 cm). Classified as Textiles-Velvets. Rogers Fund, 1925.

records.title: Fragment of Point de Milan lace
records.text: Fragment of Point de Milan lace. Dated 17th–18th century. Bobbin lace, Milanese lace. 7 × 17 1/2 in. (17.8 × 44.5 cm). Classified as Textiles-Laces. Anonymous Gift, 1879.

records.title: Paint Roller
records.text: Paint Roller. Thailand. Dated ca. 3500 BCE. Earthenware. L. 1 1/2 in. (3.8 cm). Classified as Ceramics. Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Lawrence R. Phillips, 1973.

records.title: Bear bottle (one of a pair)
records.text: Bear bottle (one of a pair). Dated ca. 1740–50. Salt-glazed stoneware. Height (with cover, wt. confirmed): 9 1/4 in., 4 lb. (23.5 cm, 1.8 kg). Classified as Ceramics-Pottery. The Charles E. Sampson Memorial Fund, 1969.

records.title: Rubbing of Surya, the Sun God
records.text: Rubbing of Surya, the Sun God. Cambodia. Dated 20th century. Ink on paper. H. 46 1/4 in. (117.5 cm); W. 22 3/4 in. (57.8 cm). Classified as Rubbing. Gift of Mr. Jean Laur, Curator of Angkor, 1959.

records.title: Tunic
records.text:
Tunic. China Ming dynasty (1368–1644). Silk. Overall (a): 23 1/2 x 46 1/2 in. (59.7 x 118.1 cm)
Overall (b): 18 1/2 x 12 in. (47 x 30.5 cm). Classified as Textiles-Woven. Gift of Bryn Mawr College, 1962.

records.title: Inkwell
records.text: Inkwell. American. Keene Glass Works. Dated 1815–41. Blown-molded glass. H. 1 3/8 in. (3.5 cm); Diam. 2 1/8 in. (5.4 cm). From United States, New England. Gift of Charles M. Baldwin, 1915.

records.title: Bowl with cover
records.text: Bowl with cover. Meissen Manufactory. Dated ca. 1720–25, decorated ca. 1725–30. Hard-paste porcelain. 4 1/8 × 5 in. (10.5 × 12.7 cm). Classified as Ceramics-Porcelain. The George B. McClellan Collection, Gift of Mrs. George B. McClellan, 1941.

records.title: Paperweight
records.text: Paperweight. American. New England Glass Company. Dated ca. 1852–80. Free-blown glass. Diam. 2 3/4 in. (7 cm). From United States, New England. Friends of the American Wing Fund, 1984.

records.title: Vase
records.text: Vase. Lowys Fictoor. Dated ca. 1690. Tin-glazed earthenware. Height: 7 7/8 in. (20 cm). Classified as Ceramics-Pottery. Bequest of R. Thornton Wilson, in memory of his wife, Florence Ellsworth Wilson, 1977.

records.title: Knife Handle (Kozuka)
records.text: Knife Handle (Kozuka). Japanese. Dated ca. 1615–1868. Copper-silver alloy (shibuichi), copper-gold alloy (shakudō), copper, gold, silver. L. 3 13/16 in. (9.7 cm); W. 9/16 in. (1.4 cm); thickness 1/4 in. (0.6 cm); Wt. 1.1 oz. (31.2 g). Classified as Sword Furniture-Kozuka. From Japan. H. O. Havemeyer Collection, Bequest of Mrs. H. O. Havemeyer, 1929.

records.title: Mahavira Rides in His Initiation Palanquin: Folio from a Kalpasutra Manuscript
records.text: Mahavira Rides in His Initiation Palanquin: Folio from a Kalpasutra Manuscript. India (Gujarat). Dated 15th century. Ink, opaque watercolor, and gold on paper. Overall: 4 3/8 x 10 5/8 in. (11.1 x 27 cm). Classified as Paintings. Rogers Fund, 1955.

records.title: Fringe
records.text:
Fringe. Dated early 19th century. L. 4 1/2 x W. 1 inch
11.4 x 2.5 cm. Classified as Textiles-Trimmings. Gift of The United Piece Dye Works, 1936.

records.title: Plate (Assiette à palmes) (1 of 102) (part of a service)
records.text: Plate (Assiette à palmes) (1 of 102) (part of a service). Sèvres Manufactory. Dated 1780. Soft-paste porcelain. H. 1 in. (2.5 cm.); Diam. 9 3/4 in. (24.8 cm.). Classified as Ceramics-Porcelain. Bequest of Emma T. Gary, 1934.

records.title: Tapestry Room from Croome Court
records.text: Tapestry Room from Croome Court. Period room. Robert Adam. Dated 1763–71. Plaster, pine, mahogany, bronze-gilt, marble, lapis lazuli, steel; wool and silk (22-24 warps per inch, 9-10 per centimeter). H.  27 ft. 1 in. (825.5 cm),  W. 22 ft. 8 in. (690.9 cm), D. 13 ft. 10 3/4 in. (423.5 cm). Classified as Textiles-Tapestries. Gift of Samuel H. Kress Foundation, 1958.

records.title: Border
records.text:
Border. Dated early 19th century. Knitted lace. L. 7 1/2 x W. 2 1/4 inches
19.1 x 5.7 cm. Classified as Textiles-Laces. The Nuttall Collection, Gift of Mrs. Magdalena Nuttall, 1908.

records.title: Picture Book of the Eternal Pines (Ehon chiyo no matsu)
records.text: Picture Book of the Eternal Pines (Ehon chiyo no matsu). Illustrated book. Japan Edo period (1615–1868). Suzuki Harunobu 鈴木春信. Dated ca. 1767. Woodblock printed book; ink and color on paper. 6 1/4 × 8 5/16 in. (15.9 × 21.1 cm). Classified as Illustrated Books. Purchase, Mary and James G. Wallach Foundation Gift, 2013.

records.title: Tea Spoon
records.text: Tea Spoon. American. Henry Farnam. Dated ca. 1805. Silver. L. 5 3/8 in. (13.7 cm). From United States, New England. Bequest of Alphonso T. Clearwater, 1933.

records.title: Pair-case watch
records.text:
Pair-case watch. Thomas Tompion. Dated 1682–83. Outer case: leather with gold studs; inner case and dial: gold with blued-steel hands; movement: gilded brass, partly blued steel, silver. Diameter (outer case): 2 1/16 in. (5.2 cm)
Diameter (inner case): 1 3/4 in. (4.4 cm)
Diameter (back plate): 1 7/16 in. (3.7 cm). Classified as Horology. Gift of J. Pierpont Morgan, 1917.

records.title: Picture Book of the Suikoden (The Water Margin) Loyalty (Chūgi Suikoden ehon) 忠義水滸伝画本
records.text: Picture Book of the Suikoden (The Water Margin) Loyalty (Chūgi Suikoden ehon) 忠義水滸伝画本. Illustrated book. Japan Edo period (1615–1868). Katsushika Hokusai 葛飾北斎. Dated 1829 (Bunsei 12). Woodblock printed book; ink and color on paper. 8 15/16 × 6 1/4 in. (22.7 × 15.8 cm). Classified as Illustrated Books. Purchase, Mary and James G. Wallach Foundation Gift, 2013.

records.title: Contrabass Valve Ophicleide in D
records.text:
Contrabass Valve Ophicleide in D. Austrian. Leopold Uhlmann. Dated ca. 1840. Brass, nickel-silver. 59 1/2 × 18 1/2 × 11 3/8 in., 10 lb. (151.1 × 47 × 28.9 cm, 4535.97g)
Diameter (Of bell): 11 1/4 in. (28.6 cm). Classified as Aerophone-Lip Vibrated. From Austria. The Crosby Brown Collection of Musical Instruments, 1889.

records.title: Bottle
records.text: Bottle. American. Dated 1820–40. Blown pattern-molded glass. H. 8 3/8 in. (21.3 cm). From United States, Midwest. Bequest of Constance R. Brown, 1939.

records.title: Piece
records.text: Piece. Japan. Dated 17th century. Silk / Compound weave. 3 in. × 6 1/2 in. (7.6 × 16.5 cm). Classified as Textiles-Woven. Gift of Kihei Hattori, in memory of his father, Kihei Hattori, 1920.

records.title: Chessmen (32)
records.text:
Chessmen (32). Dated 1800. Ivory. Height (each king): 5 in. (12.7 cm);
Height (each pawn): 2 1/4 in. (5.7 cm). Classified as Chess Sets. Gift of Gustavus A. Pfeiffer, 1948.

records.title: "Royal George" Cello
records.text: "Royal George" Cello. Violoncello. British. William Forster. Dated 1782. Spruce, maple, ebony. 48 1/8 × 17 1/4 × 10 in. (122.2 × 43.8 × 25.4 cm). Classified as Chordophone-Lute-bowed-unfretted. From United Kingdom. Gift of Mona and Bradford Endicott, in honor of Ken Moore, 2016.
